headline: Pretrained embeddings and knowledge graphs shape molecular and drug representations
label: Molecular Representation Learning
summary: Pretrained protein and chemical language model embeddings are now paired with knowledge graphs and attention for prediction.
synthesis: The dominant thread is learning task-specific representations from pretrained language-model embeddings, knowledge graphs, or curated priors, applied to molecular, protein, spectral, and biomedical data. COPTER pools protein language model residue embeddings via sliced Wasserstein optimal transport against context references, and FusionPath combines protein language model embeddings with protein domains and GO annotations to predict gene fusion pathogenicity. XRepDDA combines pretrained chemical language model embeddings with MeSH-based disease graphs and deep metric learning, while DLMVF fuses miRNA and drug attributes through attention-guided multiview learning. FLARE applies contrastive peak-node alignment for MS/MS metabolite annotation. Knowledge graphs or priors feature in Artemis, BEACON, ProMeta's pathway-guided encoding, and BioExPL's alignment of latent spaces with genetic biomarker priors. ATTNSOM contributes cross-isoform attention over a shared graph encoder for atom-level cytochrome P450 site-of-metabolism prediction. The recurring novelty is the coupling of contextual embeddings with structured biological knowledge within a single learned representation.
